title: How do we know it's working?
summary: Measure what users experience, collect logs in one place, and get alerted before customers have to tell you.

lesson.problem: After an update, card payments from one bank fail for six hours. Nothing crashes and every server looks healthy. The team finds out from angry restaurant owners on the phone.
why: They start recording metrics: numbers measured over time, like orders per minute, errors per minute and how long requests take. On a graph, the failed payments would have shown as a clear dip.
Every server now sends its logs to one place, where they can be searched. A metric tells you that something is wrong; the logs tell you why.

Finally, alerts. If orders per minute drop well below what is normal for that time of day, or errors jump, the developer on call gets a message within minutes. They keep it to a few alerts that always matter, so nobody learns to ignore them.
takeaways: Alert on what users feel (errors, slowness, fewer orders), not on every busy processor.
Metrics show that something is wrong; logs show why.
Add monitoring before you need it, not after the first outage.
